message.content:
The trapezoid has bases \(AB=20\) and \(CD=12\), with \(AB \parallel CD\).

Let the height of the trapezoid be \(h\), the perpendicular distance between the two bases.

Area of trapezoid \(ABCD\):
\[
\frac12(AB+CD)h=\frac12(20+12)h=16h
\]

Triangle \(ACB\) has base \(AB=20\). Since \(C\) lies on the line \(CD\), which is parallel to \(AB\), the height of triangle \(ACB\) from \(C\) to \(AB\) is also \(h\).

Area of triangle \(ACB\):
\[
\frac12 \cdot AB \cdot h=\frac12 \cdot 20 \cdot h=10h
\]

Thus the ratio is:
\[
\frac{10h}{16h}=\frac{5}{8}
\]

The answer is \(\frac{5}{8}\).
